newsitem.title: BULGARIA: DRUG HAULS BY BULGARIA SHOW BALKAN ROUTE REVIVAL.
newsitem.headline: DRUG HAULS BY BULGARIA SHOW BALKAN ROUTE REVIVAL.

text.p: Drug traffickers appear to be reviving the traditional "Balkan route" from Asia to Western Europe after lifting the United Nations-imposed sanctions against Yugoslavia, customs officials said on Thursday.

"Drug traffickers appear to be reviving the classical "Balkan route", which we think they abondoned during the Bosnia war," Margarita Eftimova, head of the National Customs Service's drug department told Reuters.
The route runs from Asia and Turkey through Bulgaria and Yugoslavia to Western Europe.
"Before the sanctions were lifted last year, the route from Turkey through Bulgaria and Romania was believed to be an important junction with Western Europe," Eftomova said.

Bulgaria, which lies between Turkey, Greece and Yugoslavia has seized 14.4 tonnes (31,752 lb) of drugs in 1996 against 293.3 kg (646.7 lb) in 1995, officials said. The acetic anhydride was 4,527 litres last year against 423 litres in 1995.
The figure comprises 33 hauls, of which 24 yielded 195.5 kg (431 lb) of heroin. About nine tonnes of hashish, 5.2 tonnes of marijuana and 14.3 kg (31.5 lb) of cocaine were also found.
"Last year we had two hauls of drugs in containers for the first time and this practice of the traffickers was something new for us," Eftimova said.
She said 51 traffickers from 11 nationalities were cought last year. The figure included 21 Bulgarians, 10 Turks and four Macedonians, as well as Albanians, Germans, Spaniards and Serbs.
"For the first time last year most of the traffickers were Bulgarians, operating as couriers," Eftimova said.
Bulgarian customs officers, who have siezed 42.6 tonnes of narcotics, have often complained that they lack specialised equipment to detect drugs.
"They rely mainly on their own experience, which was built up with the help of the customs administrations in Great Britain, Germany and the United States," Eftimova said.
With the help of a U.N. drug control programme, Bulgarian customs completed a well-equipped garage for customs checks at the Kapitan Andreevo checkpoint on the Turkish border, she said.

"We need funds for modern equipment especially for the Black Sea ports of Varna and Bourgas, the checkpoints on the Danube river and our western border with Yugoslavia," Eftimova said. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
